extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning benchmark for expert AGI, containing 11.5K college-level multimodal questions across 6 disciplines, 30 subjects, and 183 subfields.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was manually collected in three stages: selecting subjects from common university majors, recruiting over 50 university students (including coauthors) as annotators, and having them collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources or create new questions based on their expertise. Questions were then cleaned by authors through duplicate removal, format and typo checking, and difficulty categorization.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College textbooks, quizzes, lecture materials, and online resources; questions were also created based on annotators' expertise where necessary.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Suspected duplicates were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, then reviewed and removed by authors. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, standardized formatting was enforced, and approximately 10% of very easy problems were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Annotators were instructed to avoid questions with immediately available answers, avoid sources prohibiting copying or redistribution, ensure questions were college-level and unambiguous, and exclude very easy problems not aligning with design criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including coauthors, collected and authored multimodal questions from textbooks and online sources. The annotation protocol required each question to include one or more images, be in English, be college-level, be categorized as multiple-choice or open-ended, and include question text, answer options if applicable, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanation if available. A secondary review team validated annotations, and ambiguities were discussed collaboratively.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification was developed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were categorized by difficulty (very easy, easy, medium, hard). Duplicate detection used lexical overlap and source URL similarity. In error analysis, 150 GPT-4V errors were manually annotated by expert annotators using knowledge and golden explanations when available.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including coauthors, specializing in the relevant majors; 90 college senior students were used as human experts for evaluation (3 per subject).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OCR by MMOCR; captioning by LLaVA-1.5; regular expressions and response-processing workflows were used for evaluation answer extraction.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioned releases with a change log from V1 to V4; V4 updated results, model names, added human expert results, and fixed errors. The live-updating leaderboard is maintained at the project website.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None explicitly collected; annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions containing private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to monitor progress toward Expert AGI and may help develop next-generation multimodal foundation models, while also highlighting potential risks of job displacement and economic disruption associated with Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The benchmark also reflects subject and image-type coverage choices, and the authors note that college-level subjects may not fully represent Expert AGI tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping between MMMU performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, and college exams are not the only tasks an AGI should tackle. The benchmark may also carry biases from manual curation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, evaluation, validation, and testing of multimodal models; zero-shot evaluation is emphasized, with some few-shot results reported. The dataset is also intended to stimulate development of next-generation multimodal foundation models.
